definitions.explanation: A short stick passed between runners in a relay race. Also used figuratively for passing on a role, responsibility, or tradition to the next person.

examples.japanese: バトン⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{落|お}として→落とす：01246_otosu⟧⟦{順位|じゅんい}→順位：14679_juni⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{下|さ}がった→下がる：01188_sagaru⟧。
examples.english: We dropped the baton and fell in the rankings.

examples.japanese: ⟦{先輩|せんぱい}→先輩：01451_senpai⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{後輩|こうはい}→後輩：02501_kouhai⟧⟦へ→へ：02473_he⟧バトン⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{渡|わた}す→渡す：02442_watasu⟧よう⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧、⟦{伝統|でんとう}→伝統：09585_dentou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{受|う}け{継|つ}がれている→受け継ぐ：06700_uketsugu⟧。
examples.english: Traditions are carried on, as if passing the baton from seniors to juniors.

notes:
USAGE:
バトン⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{渡|わた}す→渡す：02442_watasu⟧ (to pass the baton) is extremely common both literally (in relay races) and figuratively (handing over responsibility). The figurative use appears frequently in business and organizational contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- バトン⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{渡|わた}す→渡す：02442_watasu⟧: to pass the baton
- バトン⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{受|う}け{取|と}る→受け取る：01883_uketoru⟧: to receive the baton
- バトン⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{落|お}とす→落とす：01246_otosu⟧: to drop the baton
- バトンタッチ: handover, passing the baton (wasei-eigo)
- バトンパス: baton pass (in relay races)

バトンタッチ is a wasei-eigo expression meaning a smooth handover of duties. It is not used in English.
